question.text: What is used to set a road's proper speed limit, and which limits must you obey?

answer.text: Road conditions, traffic flow and the number of crashes are used to set a road's proper speed limit, and you must obey every posted limit.

teaching.text: A road's proper limit is set from road conditions, traffic flow and crash numbers, and every posted limit must be obeyed. Remember: obey every posted limit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Road conditions, traffic flow and the number of crashes are used to set a road's proper speed limit, and you must obey every posted limit.

question.text: With no posted limit, what is the speed limit approaching a school crosswalk?

answer.text: When no limit is posted, the speed limit is fifteen miles per hour as you approach a school crosswalk.

teaching.text: With no sign posted, the limit is fifteen miles per hour as you approach a school crosswalk. Remember: fifteen near school crosswalks.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When no limit is posted, the speed limit is fifteen miles per hour as you approach a school crosswalk.

question.text: With no posted limit, what is the speed limit in a business or residential district?

answer.text: When no limit is posted, the speed limit is twenty-five miles per hour in any business or residential district.

teaching.text: With no sign posted, the limit is twenty-five miles per hour in a business or residential district. Remember: twenty-five in town.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When no limit is posted, the speed limit is twenty-five miles per hour in any business or residential district.

question.text: How do the unposted limits near a school crosswalk and in a district compare?

answer.text: A school crosswalk approach defaults to fifteen miles per hour, while a business or residential district defaults to twenty-five miles per hour

teaching.text: With no sign, a school crosswalk approach is fifteen miles per hour, while a business or residential district is twenty-five. Remember: fifteen versus twenty-five.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A school crosswalk approach defaults to fifteen miles per hour, while a business or residential district defaults to twenty-five miles per hour

question.text: With no posted limit, what is the speed limit on open highways or city freeways?

answer.text: When no limit is posted, the speed limit is fifty-five miles per hour on open highways or city freeways.

teaching.text: With no sign posted, open highways and city freeways have a limit of fifty-five miles per hour. Remember: fifty-five on open highways.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When no limit is posted, the speed limit is fifty-five miles per hour on open highways or city freeways.

question.text: With no posted limit, what is the speed limit on designated open highways?

answer.text: When no limit is posted, the speed limit is sixty-five miles per hour on designated open highways.

teaching.text: With no sign posted, designated open highways have a limit of sixty-five miles per hour. Remember: sixty-five where designated.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When no limit is posted, the speed limit is sixty-five miles per hour on designated open highways.

question.text: With no posted limit, what is the speed limit on rural freeways?

answer.text: When no limit is posted, the speed limit is seventy-five miles per hour on rural freeways.

teaching.text: With no sign posted, rural freeways have a limit of seventy-five miles per hour. Remember: seventy-five on rural freeways.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When no limit is posted, the speed limit is seventy-five miles per hour on rural freeways.

question.text: How do the unposted limits for open highways, designated open highways and rural freeways compare?

answer.text: Open highways and city freeways default to fifty-five miles per hour, designated open highways to sixty-five miles per hour, and rural freeways to seventy-five miles per hour

teaching.text: With no sign, open highways and city freeways are fifty-five, designated open highways sixty-five, and rural freeways seventy-five miles per hour. Remember: fifty-five, sixty-five, seventy-five.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Open highways and city freeways default to fifty-five miles per hour, designated open highways to sixty-five miles per hour, and rural freeways to seventy-five miles per hour

question.text: What does a white speed limit sign with black letters show?

answer.text: A white speed limit sign with black letters is a regulatory sign showing the highest speed you may legally drive.

teaching.text: A white speed sign with black letters is a regulatory sign that shows the fastest you may legally go. Remember: white is the legal maximum.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A white speed limit sign with black letters is a regulatory sign showing the highest speed you may legally drive.

question.text: What does an orange sign with black letters give?

answer.text: An orange sign with black letters gives a recommended safe speed for a curve, a grade or another special condition, so slow down until you are sure you can get through safely.

teaching.text: An orange sign with black letters gives a recommended safe speed for a curve, a grade or another special condition, so slow down until you can get through safely. Remember: orange is advice.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An orange sign with black letters gives a recommended safe speed for a curve, a grade or another special condition, so slow down until you are sure you can get through safely.

question.text: How does a white speed sign differ from an orange one?

answer.text: A white sign with black letters is the legal maximum, while an orange sign with black letters is only a recommended safe speed for that spot.

teaching.text: A white sign with black letters is the legal maximum, while an orange sign with black letters is only a recommended safe speed for that spot. Remember: white is law, orange advice.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A white sign with black letters is the legal maximum, while an orange sign with black letters is only a recommended safe speed for that spot.

question.text: What do speed limits assume, and what should you do in bad weather?

answer.text: Speed limits assume the best driving conditions, so in bad weather lower your speed to one that is reasonable.

teaching.text: Limits are set for the best conditions, so in bad weather drop to a speed that is reasonable. Remember: limits assume ideal conditions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Speed limits assume the best driving conditions, so in bad weather lower your speed to one that is reasonable.

question.text: How should you adjust your speed on wet, snowy or icy roads?

answer.text: On wet roads, and on roads with snow or ice, reduce your speed appropriately.

teaching.text: Slow down appropriately on wet roads and on roads with snow or ice. Remember: slow down appropriately.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On wet roads, and on roads with snow or ice, reduce your speed appropriately.

question.text: Besides slowing down, what should you do with your following distance in bad weather?

answer.text: In bad weather, double your following distance from the vehicle ahead as well as slowing down.

teaching.text: When the weather is bad, slow down and also double the distance to the vehicle ahead. Remember: double the gap.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In bad weather, double your following distance from the vehicle ahead as well as slowing down.

question.text: Is slowing down alone enough in bad weather?

answer.text: Bad weather calls for both a lower speed and twice the usual following distance, not just one of them.

teaching.text: Bad weather calls for a lower speed and double the usual following distance together, not just one of them. Remember: slower and farther back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Bad weather calls for both a lower speed and twice the usual following distance, not just one of them.

question.text: Can driving too slowly be dangerous?

answer.text: Driving too slowly can be just as dangerous as driving too fast.

teaching.text: Going too slowly can be every bit as dangerous as going too fast. Remember: too slow can be dangerous.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Driving too slowly can be just as dangerous as driving too fast.

question.text: Where should you drive when you are slower than traffic?

answer.text: Whenever you are slower than the traffic around you, keep to the right lane and let faster vehicles pass.

teaching.text: Any time you are slower than the traffic around you, keep right and let faster vehicles pass. Remember: slower keeps right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Whenever you are slower than the traffic around you, keep to the right lane and let faster vehicles pass.

question.text: What do traffic signs do?

answer.text: Traffic signs control traffic and give drivers important information.

teaching.text: Traffic signs control traffic and give drivers information they need. Remember: control and inform.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Traffic signs control traffic and give drivers important information.

question.text: What can a sign's shape tell you?

answer.text: A sign's shape can tell you as much about its meaning as its color or its words.

teaching.text: The shape of a sign can tell you as much as its color or its wording. Remember: shape has meaning.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A sign's shape can tell you as much about its meaning as its color or its words.

question.text: When may a sign's shape be the only part you can make out?

answer.text: In heavy rain, dust storms or fog, the shape may be the only part of a sign you can make out.

teaching.text: In heavy rain, dust storms or fog, a sign's shape may be the only thing you can see. Remember: rain, dust, fog: read shapes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In heavy rain, dust storms or fog, the shape may be the only part of a sign you can make out.

question.text: Which signs use the octagon shape, and what do they require?

answer.text: The octagon shape is used only for stop signs, which require a complete stop.

teaching.text: Only stop signs use the octagon shape, and they require a complete stop. Remember: octagon means full stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The octagon shape is used only for stop signs, which require a complete stop.

question.text: What does a triangle-shaped sign require?

answer.text: A triangle-shaped sign requires you to yield the right-of-way to cross traffic or merging traffic.

teaching.text: A triangle-shaped sign tells you to yield the right-of-way to cross traffic or merging traffic. Remember: triangle means yield.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A triangle-shaped sign requires you to yield the right-of-way to cross traffic or merging traffic.

question.text: How does an octagon differ from a triangle?

answer.text: An octagon always means stop, while a triangle means yield to cross or merging traffic.

teaching.text: An octagon always means stop, while a triangle means yield to cross or merging traffic. Remember: stop versus yield.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An octagon always means stop, while a triangle means yield to cross or merging traffic.

question.text: What do rectangular regulatory signs do?

answer.text: Rectangular regulatory signs control traffic and direct your speed and direction, such as go straight or turn left, no U-turn, no left turn and no right turn.

teaching.text: Rectangular regulatory signs control traffic and direct speed and direction, such as no U-turn or no left turn. Remember: rectangles set rules.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Rectangular regulatory signs control traffic and direct your speed and direction, such as go straight or turn left, no U-turn, no left turn and no right turn.

question.text: What do turn, curve and winding road signs warn of?

answer.text: Turn, curve and winding road signs warn drivers of bends in the roadway ahead.

teaching.text: Turn, curve and winding road signs warn you that the road bends ahead. Remember: bends ahead.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Turn, curve and winding road signs warn drivers of bends in the roadway ahead.

question.text: What do small yellow square signs mounted below a curve sign show?

answer.text: Small yellow square signs may be mounted below a curve sign to show the safe speed through the curve.

teaching.text: A small yellow square sign under a curve sign may show the safe speed for that curve. Remember: plate shows curve speed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Small yellow square signs may be mounted below a curve sign to show the safe speed through the curve.

question.text: Which sign shows the safe speed through a curve?

answer.text: The small yellow square that may sit under a curve sign is the one that shows the safe speed through that curve, while the curve sign itself only warns of the bend.

teaching.text: The small yellow square under a curve sign shows the safe curve speed, while the curve sign itself only warns of the bend. Remember: the small plate.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The small yellow square that may sit under a curve sign is the one that shows the safe speed through that curve, while the curve sign itself only warns of the bend.

question.text: What does a pennant-shaped sign mark?

answer.text: A pennant-shaped sign marks where a no-passing zone begins.

teaching.text: A pennant-shaped sign shows where a no-passing zone starts. Remember: pennant starts no passing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A pennant-shaped sign marks where a no-passing zone begins.

question.text: What do yellow diamond-shaped signs warn of?

answer.text: Yellow diamond-shaped signs warn of a possible danger ahead.

teaching.text: Yellow diamond-shaped signs warn that there may be danger ahead. Remember: diamond warns of danger.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yellow diamond-shaped signs warn of a possible danger ahead.

question.text: How does a pennant differ from a yellow diamond?

answer.text: A pennant marks the start of a no-passing zone, while a yellow diamond warns of a possible hazard ahead.

teaching.text: A pennant marks where a no-passing zone starts, while a yellow diamond warns of possible danger ahead. Remember: no passing versus danger.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A pennant marks the start of a no-passing zone, while a yellow diamond warns of a possible hazard ahead.

question.text: What does a permanent pentagon-shaped school crossing sign warn of?

answer.text: A permanent five-sided, pentagon-shaped school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing at any time of day.

teaching.text: A permanent five-sided school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing at any time of day. Remember: pentagon means school.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A permanent five-sided, pentagon-shaped school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing at any time of day.

question.text: What colors may school crossing signs be?

answer.text: School crossing signs may be yellow, and many Arizona school districts are posting yellow-green ones.

teaching.text: School crossing signs may be yellow, and many Arizona school districts now post yellow-green ones. Remember: yellow or yellow-green.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: School crossing signs may be yellow, and many Arizona school districts are posting yellow-green ones.

question.text: What is the top speed between the first portable school sign and the school crossing sign?

answer.text: You must also obey portable signs sometimes set in the middle of the road, and from the first sign until past the school crossing sign the top speed is fifteen miles per hour

teaching.text: Obey portable signs placed in the road, and from the first one until you pass the school crossing sign, the top speed is fifteen miles per hour. Remember: fifteen through the zone.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You must also obey portable signs sometimes set in the middle of the road, and from the first sign until past the school crossing sign the top speed is fifteen miles per hour

question.text: What speed limit applies when the portable school signs are not out?

answer.text: When the portable school signs are not out, the area's normal speed limit applies.

teaching.text: When the portable school signs are not set out, the area's normal speed limit is in effect. Remember: no portable signs, normal limit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When the portable school signs are not out, the area's normal speed limit applies.

question.text: When does the fifteen miles per hour school limit apply?

answer.text: The school-zone limit of fifteen miles per hour runs from the first portable sign until past the crossing sign, and it lapses when those portable signs are removed.

teaching.text: The fifteen miles per hour school limit runs from the first portable sign until past the crossing sign, and it lapses when those signs are taken away. Remember: only with portable signs out.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The school-zone limit of fifteen miles per hour runs from the first portable sign until past the crossing sign, and it lapses when those portable signs are removed.

question.text: May you pass another vehicle in a school crossing zone?

answer.text: Passing another vehicle in a school crossing zone is prohibited.

teaching.text: Passing another vehicle is not allowed in a school crossing zone. Remember: no passing near schools.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Passing another vehicle in a school crossing zone is prohibited.

question.text: What must you do at a school crossing with a crossing guard?

answer.text: Follow the crossing guard's instructions and stop completely whenever anyone is in the crosswalk.

teaching.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions and stop completely whenever anyone is in the crosswalk. Remember: follow the guard.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Follow the crossing guard's instructions and stop completely whenever anyone is in the crosswalk.

question.text: What does a circle-shaped railroad warning sign tell you?

answer.text: A circle-shaped railroad warning sign tells you a railroad crossing is ahead.

teaching.text: A circle-shaped railroad warning sign tells you a railroad crossing is coming up. Remember: circle means railroad ahead.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A circle-shaped railroad warning sign tells you a railroad crossing is ahead.

question.text: Which shape marks a school crossing, and which a railroad warning?

answer.text: A pentagon is the school crossing shape, while a circle is the railroad warning shape.

teaching.text: A pentagon marks a school crossing, while a circle warns of a railroad crossing. Remember: pentagon school, circle rail.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A pentagon is the school crossing shape, while a circle is the railroad warning shape.

question.text: What does the railroad crossing sign mark?

answer.text: The railroad crossing sign marks the exact location of the crossing.

teaching.text: The railroad crossing sign sits at the exact spot where the tracks cross the road. Remember: marks the exact crossing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The railroad crossing sign marks the exact location of the crossing.

question.text: How close to the nearest rail may you stop when warnings show a train is coming?

answer.text: Stop no closer than fifteen feet from the nearest rail when you see flashing red lights, a lowered barricade, ringing bells or a flagger warning of a train or other on-track equipment.

teaching.text: With flashing red lights, a lowered barricade, ringing bells or a flagger warning of a train, stop at least fifteen feet from the nearest rail. Remember: fifteen feet back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Stop no closer than fifteen feet from the nearest rail when you see flashing red lights, a lowered barricade, ringing bells or a flagger warning of a train or other on-track equipment.

question.text: How many railroad warnings does it take to require a stop?

answer.text: At a railroad crossing, any one of flashing red lights, a lowered barricade, ringing bells or a flagger is enough to require stopping at least fifteen feet from the nearest rail.

teaching.text: Any single railroad warning, whether lights, a barricade, bells or a flagger, means stopping at least fifteen feet from the nearest rail. Remember: any one warning.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a railroad crossing, any one of flashing red lights, a lowered barricade, ringing bells or a flagger is enough to require stopping at least fifteen feet from the nearest rail.

question.text: What two different things does the number fifteen measure in this section?

answer.text: The school crossing speed and the railroad stopping distance share the number fifteen but measure different things, miles per hour versus feet.

teaching.text: Fifteen shows up twice: as the school crossing speed in miles per hour and as the railroad stopping distance in feet. Remember: miles per hour versus feet.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The school crossing speed and the railroad stopping distance share the number fifteen but measure different things, miles per hour versus feet.

question.text: When may you cross the tracks after a warning?

answer.text: Do not cross the tracks until every signal has stopped and the barricade has risen all the way.

teaching.text: Do not cross until every signal has stopped and the barricade has gone all the way up. Remember: signals off, gate up.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not cross the tracks until every signal has stopped and the barricade has risen all the way.

question.text: May you drive around or under a lowered crossing barricade?

answer.text: Never drive around or under a lowered crossing barricade.

teaching.text: Never go around or under a crossing barricade that is down. Remember: never around the gate.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never drive around or under a lowered crossing barricade.

question.text: What should you assume about trains at any crossing?

answer.text: Assume that a train or other rail equipment could be coming on any track, at any hour.

teaching.text: Assume a train or other rail equipment could be coming on any track at any time. Remember: any track, any hour.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Assume that a train or other rail equipment could be coming on any track, at any hour.

question.text: What should you never let happen at a railroad crossing?

answer.text: Never let yourself get trapped on a railroad crossing.

teaching.text: Never let your vehicle end up trapped on a railroad crossing. Remember: never get trapped.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never let yourself get trapped on a railroad crossing.

question.text: What should you do if your vehicle stalls on the tracks?

answer.text: If your vehicle stalls on the tracks, get out of it.

teaching.text: If your vehicle stalls on the tracks, get out of it. Remember: stalled on tracks, get out.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If your vehicle stalls on the tracks, get out of it.

question.text: What is the manual's rule if your vehicle stalls on the tracks?

answer.text: If a vehicle stalls on the tracks, the rule the manual gives is simply to get out of it.

teaching.text: If your vehicle stalls on the tracks, the manual's rule is simply to get out of it. Remember: just get out.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If a vehicle stalls on the tracks, the rule the manual gives is simply to get out of it.

hooks_spoken: With no posted limit: fifteen near a school crosswalk, twenty-five in a district, and fifty-five, sixty-five or seventy-five on highways and freeways.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of speed limits when none is posted. With no posted limit: fifteen near a school crosswalk, twenty-five in a district, and fifty-five, sixty-five or seventy-five on highways and freeways. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: White signs are the legal maximum and orange signs give advice; in bad weather slow down and double your following distance.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of speed signs and conditions. White signs are the legal maximum and orange signs give advice; in bad weather slow down and double your following distance. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Octagon stops, triangle yields, pennant starts no passing, diamond warns, and the small plate under a curve sign shows its safe speed.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of what sign shapes mean. Octagon stops, triangle yields, pennant starts no passing, diamond warns, and the small plate under a curve sign shows its safe speed. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: The fifteen miles per hour school limit runs from the first portable sign past the crossing sign, and passing is not allowed in the zone.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of school crossings. The fifteen miles per hour school limit runs from the first portable sign past the crossing sign, and passing is not allowed in the zone. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: At any one railroad warning, stop at least fifteen feet from the rail, never go around a lowered gate, and get out if you stall on the tracks.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of railroad crossings. At any one railroad warning, stop at least fifteen feet from the rail, never go around a lowered gate, and get out if you stall on the tracks. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.
